subject: Shit To Do in NYC (Nov 16): Stevie Wonder, Heems, Crown Heights dembow
opener: Last normal week before Thanksgiving eats the calendar, and it is a good one: a legend doing a whole album at the Garden on your Thursday, two guys whose records you own improvising for 29 bucks in Bushwick, and the Botanic Garden lights switching on Friday before the holiday mob shows up. One club night this week, on purpose. The rest is rooms you have never been sent to.

picks.headline: Stevie Wonder, full album, the Garden, Thursday
picks.title: Stevie Wonder: Songs in the Key of Life 50th Anniversary
picks.why: Songs in the Key of Life front to back for the 50th, on your main night out. Your library is thick with Bill Withers, Nat King Cole, Etta James; this is the living source of all of it. You do the big-spectacle thing a few times a year and this is the one your wife will talk about the way she talks about the Nutcracker. The Garden is a twenty-minute ride, not a tourist errand.
picks.heads_up: Ticket prices were not posted where we could read them, so assume arena-legend money. 8pm start means the sitter is booked past eleven.
picks.invite_text: Stevie Wonder is doing Songs in the Key of Life front to back at the Garden on Thursday. Want me to grab tickets and line up the sitter?

verification.note: Ticketmaster page would not load, but the BrooklynVegan NYC 11/19/26 calendar page I read lists 'Stevie Wonder Songs in The Key of Life Performances 50th Anniversary' at Madison Square Garden, 8:00PM, linking to the same Ticketmaster event ID; no price shown.

picks.headline: Heems and Lee Ranaldo improvise, 200 people
picks.title: VEENA.NYC presents IN IMPROVISATION ft. Heems, Lee Ranaldo, Hisham Bharoocha & more
picks.why: This is the shape you keep saying the email misses: people whose records you know, in a room of 200, doing something that exists for one night only. Heems from Das Racist and Lee Ranaldo from Sonic Youth, no setlist, no second show. Twenty-nine dollars is two drinks. Friday in Bushwick, no tourist energy anywhere near it.
picks.heads_up: About $29, 21+, 8pm start. One night only and no second announcement, so buy before Friday.
picks.invite_text: Friday in Bushwick: Heems and Lee Ranaldo from Sonic Youth doing a one-off improvised set at the Sultan Room, like 30 bucks. You in?

verification.note: Read the BrooklynVegan/DoNYC event page: VEENA.NYC presents IN IMPROVISATION at The Sultan Room, Fri Nov 20 2026, 8:00PM, $28.67, 21+ — matches the listing.

picks.headline: Dembow and amapiano till 4am, Crown Heights
picks.title: Algo. Riddim: Epic B & Uproot Andy (QUENCH)
picks.price: $5 online (limited), $10 at the door before midnight
picks.why: Afrobeats and dancehall is your current phase and this is the resident-run version of it, not a promoter with a table chart. Epic B and Uproot Andy have been doing this for years: dembow, dancehall, amapiano, gqom, kuduro, no requests. Friends and Lovers is a neighborhood bar fifteen minutes from your door where you can still get to the bartender.
picks.heads_up: $5 if you buy online, $10 at the door before midnight. It runs to 4am, so show up at midnight and leave whenever your Sunday needs you to.
picks.invite_text: Saturday night, Crown Heights: dancehall and amapiano at Friends and Lovers, ten bucks at the door. Meet around midnight?

verification.note: Read the Friends and Lovers (fnlbk.com) event page: Saturday, November 21, 2026 10:00 PM to Sunday 4:00 AM, $10 general admission before 12AM, $5 online (limited) — all matches.

picks.headline: Bridget Everett, 180 seats, Joe's Pub
picks.title: Bridget Everett & The Tender Moments at Joe's Pub
picks.when: Tue Nov 17 to Fri Nov 20, doors 9pm
picks.price: $85 to $135, plus a two-drink or one-food minimum
picks.why: A face you know from HBO doing loud, filthy cabaret with a live band in a room the size of a living room. These four nights were sold out and they just released more. It is a better babysitter night than another burlesque run, and it is the small-room trade you actually like: big name, no distance between you and the stage.
picks.heads_up: $85 to $135 plus a two-drink or one-food minimum, doors 9pm. The released batch is small and these nights already sold once. Could not re-check the listing page this morning. Confirm the date on the link before you buy.
picks.invite_text: Bridget Everett is doing four nights at Joe's Pub with her band and they just released more tickets. Thursday or Friday, your call?

verification.note: publictheater.org blocks fetching (url_not_allowed); search results from Joe's Pub's own calendar show a Nov 17–20 run for Bridget Everett & The Tender Moments and the prior-year page shows $85–$135 with doors 9PM and a 2-drink/1-food minimum, but I could not read the 2026 event page itself, so this is snippet-level only.

picks.headline: Drag bingo in a tiny Bushwick bar
picks.title: Variety Show Bingo at The Tiny Cupboard
picks.why: A bar doing genuinely weird programming: drag host, bingo, a guest from Taipei and somebody's first ever stand-up set, in a room that holds maybe forty people. Runs 6:30 to 8:30, so it is a Thursday a dad can actually do. Nobody in the group chat has heard of this, which is the point.
picks.heads_up: The only listing is the host's own Instagram, so confirm it is still on before anyone drives out. Early door, bring cash for the bar.
picks.invite_text: Thursday at 6:30 in Bushwick there's a drag bingo variety thing in a tiny bar, done by 8:30. Cheap and weird, come with me.

verification.note: Instagram is not fetchable, but I read the GO Magazine venue calendar for The Tiny Cupboard Comedy Club (10 Cooper St), which lists the recurring 'Drag Bingo & Open Set Variety Show!' on November 19 @ 6:30 pm - 8:30 pm; the Eventbrite series page confirms it is a weekly Thursday 6:30–8:30pm show; no price stated.

picks.headline: Fellowship of the Ring, 35mm, brunch
picks.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring, 25th anniversary on 35mm
picks.when: Sat Nov 21 to Sun Nov 22, brunch screenings, late morning
picks.why: You ticked Nitehawk themed screenings and this is the best version of it: the theatrical cut on an actual 35mm print, food and drinks at your seat, done by mid-afternoon. A three-hour movie with two friends and no sitter math. Saturday or Sunday both work.
picks.heads_up: Nitehawk posted on Nov 15 that seats are nearly gone, so book today. It is the three-hour theatrical cut, so plan the morning around it. Could not re-check the listing page this morning. Confirm the date on the link before you buy.
picks.invite_text: Saturday brunch: Fellowship of the Ring on 35mm at Nitehawk Prospect Park, food at your seat. Grabbing tickets today before it sells out.

verification.note: The Instagram URL cannot be fetched and nitehawkcinema.com pages were not retrievable; search results (Nitehawk's own 35mm/brunch series pages and the Brooklyn CB6 venue calendar showing 'November 21 @ 11:00 am - 2:15 pm' at Nitehawk Prospect Park) support the Nov 21 late-morning 35mm brunch screening, but I could not read a page directly to confirm showtime or price.

picks.headline: Lightscape opens Friday, before the crush
picks.title: Lightscape 2026 opening weekend
picks.when: Fri Nov 20 to Sun Jan 3, after dark, timed entry slots through the evening; the trail is about a mile and takes roughly an hour
picks.price: peak entry $44 adults, $28 children; Anytime Entry $59; under 2 free
picks.why: You already rate the Botanic Garden light trail as one of the better nights you have had here. Opening weekend is the one stretch where it isn't shoulder-to-shoulder with December. An early timed slot works with the one-year-old in a carrier, and a late one is a perfectly good forty-minute date before dinner.
picks.heads_up: Timed entry, roughly a mile outside and about an hour. $44 adult peak, $28 child, $59 for an anytime slot, under 2 free. Dress for standing in the cold.
picks.invite_text: Lightscape at the Botanic Garden opens Friday. Want to do an early slot this weekend before it turns into a December mob scene?

verification.note: Read bbg.org/lightscape: Lightscape runs November 20, 2026–January 3, 2027 at Brooklyn Botanic Garden with staggered timed entry; ticket table confirms Peak adult $44, child (3–11) $28, Anytime Entry $59, baby 0–2 free, prices include fees; the page does not print specific entry-slot times.

anytime.title: The Collectors Bar

anytime.headline: Jalopy: 100 wooden seats, roots and klezmer
anytime.title: Jalopy Theatre family and roots programming
anytime.when: varies; family shows usually weekend late morning or early afternoon
anytime.venue: Jalopy Theatre and School of Music
anytime.why: A hundred-seat room on the Carroll Gardens edge of Red Hook doing old-time, roots and klezmer-adjacent bills, plus occasional daytime family shows. It is the one venue that can give you a klezmer night and a toddler show in the same month. Check their calendar before you commit to a date.

verification.note: jalopy.biz redirects to jalopytheatre.org, which loaded and confirms the venue and its ongoing programming (performance calendar, open mic, adult and Jalopy Jr classes) at the Carroll Gardens/Red Hook location; the linked upcoming-performances calendar returned no listings, so the 'often under $20' price claim is not verified.

family.headline: The Pop Ups play the Jewish Museum, Sunday 11:30
family.title: Family Concert: The Pop Ups + Princess Backpack and Benjamin
family.price: $24 adult, free for kids 18 and under, includes museum admission
family.why: A Grammy-nominated kids' band in a real auditorium rather than a church basement, one hour, done by 12:30, and the ticket includes museum admission so you can walk a gallery after. Sits squarely in the Jewish-culture lane you ticked, and it is verified.
family.invite_text: Sunday morning there's a kids' band playing a proper auditorium at the Jewish Museum, 11:30 to 12:30, and museum entry is included. Want to take him?

verification.note: Read The Jewish Museum program page: Nov. 22, 2026, 11:30 am–12:30 pm, The Pop Ups + Princess Backpack and Benjamin, $24 adult ($20 family members), free for children 18 and under, includes museum admission — all matches.

notes: The body lane came back with nothing this week, so no sauna or plunge pick; it should be back once December cold sets in. I left Nutcracker Rouge out on purpose, you have had Company XIV twice this fall and it runs to late January. One booking update: if you want New York City Ballet's Nutcracker with her, the good Saturday evenings are already thinning out, so buy this week. The body research lane failed this week, so that side is thin.
